title: Ramesh Chandra Gupta v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Arun Tandon, J.; Harsh Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to s.127 / Supply Code forum.
headnote: A writ challenging an Executive Engineer's 2010 theft-assessment demand was dismissed. The High Court held that if the consumer is dissatisfied with the demand, the remedy is an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or the appropriate forum under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: The petitioner, a consumer of Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd., sought quashing of the Executive Engineer's order dated 2 January 2010 recording theft of electricity and raising an assessment. That order followed directions in his earlier Writ Petition No. 56168 of 2009, decided on 27 September 2009. In August 2010 the Court allowed an amendment and directed reconnection on deposit of half of arrears of Rs 65,863, with future bills to be paid. The writ, filed in 2010, continued without an interim order.

holding_units.holding: A writ petition challenging an Executive Engineer's order recording theft of electricity and raising an assessment will not be examined on merits; the consumer must proceed under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or before the appropriate forum under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: correctness of the 2 January 2010 theft finding and assessment demand
not_decided.note: Left to Section 127 or the Supply Code 2005 forum.
